title: The circle packing
reference: Levine, Pegden and Smart, "Apollonian structure in the Abelian sandpile" and "The Apollonian structure of integer superharmonic matrices", Ann. of Math. 186 (2017) 1-67
about: The integer superharmonic matrices on Z^2 -- which decide which periodic patches appear in the sandpile scaling limit -- are in bijection with the circles of an Apollonian circle packing. Stored here are two charts of one packing: the Apollonian band packing in its primitive integral normalisation, and its image under an inversion, the standard bounded integral gasket.
encoding: Every circle is an exact integer triple (k, p, q): curvature k, centre (p/k, q/k), radius 1/|k|. Equivalently the Lagarias-Mallows-Wilks curvature-centre w = k*z = p + q*i is a Gaussian integer, so the packing is integer data throughout. Each chart is depths[d] for d = 0 .. maxdepth, one entry per generation of the Descartes recursion, holding parallel arrays k[], p[], q[] sorted by (|k|, p, q). Two culls fall out of that layout: within a depth, |k| is ascending, so a renderer breaks out of the inner loop the moment scale/|k| drops below a pixel; and depths run coarse-to-fine, so drawing them in order refines the picture progressively. Depth is a generation count, not a size bound: a single depth spans many scales, so cull on |k|, and use depth only for draw order and for colouring by generation.
grow: Descartes reflection is exact in Z and Z[i]: for a tangent quadruple (a,b,c,d) the circle inscribed in the curvilinear triangle (a,b,c) is e = 2(a+b+c) - d componentwise, and that triangle splits into (a,b,e), (b,c,e), (a,c,e) with outer partners c, a, b. Every circle inside a triangle has curvature at least that of its inscribed circle, so pruning at k > kmax is exact and each circle is produced once. Run the same three lines in the browser to go deeper than kmax and zoom without limit.
zoom: To zoom past kmax, recurse from "seed" and cull the recursion, not the output. Two exact prunes make it rigorous. (1) SIZE: every circle inside the curvilinear triangle (a,b,c) has curvature at least that of the inscribed circle e = 2(a+b+c) - d, so once 1/e.k is under a pixel the whole subtree is. (2) VIEWPORT: two tangent circles a, b touch at ((a.p+b.p)/(a.k+b.k), (a.q+b.q)/(a.k+b.k)) -- exact, and valid for the outer circle too because its curvature is negative. Those three tangency points are the vertices of the curvilinear triangle, whose three sides bow inward, so the triangle and every descendant circle lie inside their straight triangle; if that triangle misses the view, prune. With both prunes the work per frame is proportional to what is on screen, and the zoom has no floor other than double precision (about 10^15 in scale, which is around curvature 10^15 -- far past anything drawable). One drawing caveat: deep in, the few enclosing circles are enormous relative to the view, so stroke them as the arc clipped to the viewport rather than as a full circle -- a path whose radius is millions of pixels loses precision and can come out as a straight line.
labels: Each circle carries two integer curvatures, one per chart. For a gasket circle (k,p,q) the Lagarias-Mallows-Wilks co-curvature kbar = (p*p + q*q - 1)/k is an integer (k*kbar = |w|^2 - 1) and is exactly the curvature of the same circle in the band chart; kbar = 0 for the two circles (2,0,1) and (2,0,-1), which are the images of the band's two boundary lines. Conversely a band circle (k,p,q) has gasket curvature (p*p + (q-k)^2 - 1)/k. Gasket curvatures are 1 (the outer circle) or 2, 3, 6, 11 mod 12; band curvatures are 0 or 1 mod 4.

gasket.coords: The unit disc |z| <= 1 centred at the origin, y upward. The outer circle is the triple (-1,0,0): its negative curvature records that the packing lies inside it, and it should be drawn with radius 1. Every other circle has k > 0.
gasket.symmetry: Invariant under (p,q) -> (p,-q) and (p,q) -> (-p,q), so the stored set is closed under both reflections.

band.coords: The strip 0 <= y <= 2, invariant under z -> z + 2. Only the fundamental period is stored: centres with 0 <= x < 2, i.e. 0 <= p < 2k. Tile by (k,p,q) -> (k, p + 2*n*k, q) for n in Z. The two boundary lines y = 0 and y = 2 are the curvature-0 members of the same packing; they are listed under "lines" because k = 0 cannot encode a centre. This normalisation is primitive: the gcd of all curvatures is 1, so these curvatures are the arithmetic labels.

charts.map: w = 1/(z - i) carries the band chart onto the gasket chart; z = i + 1/w carries it back. It is the inversion about the centre of the band circle |z - i| = 1, which becomes the gasket outer circle. The two charts below are generated independently as integer data and checked against each other.
charts.checked: band |z-i|=1 -> curvature -1; band line y=0 -> (2,0,1); band line y=2 -> (2,0,-1); band |z-2-i|=1 -> (3,2,0).
